sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于对设计的热爱以及围绕设计的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片做DJ的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，摆满了精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: My dream catcher?
sentences.zh: 我的捕梦网？

sentences.en: Oh, it's called a dream catcher, so I guess it like catches bad dreams but hasn't been working so good.
sentences.zh: 哦，它叫捕梦网，所以我猜它应该是用来捕捉噩梦的，但好像效果不太好。

sentences.en: Oh yeah?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.zh: 你最近做噩梦了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I've had some last night.
sentences.zh: 是的，昨晚做了一些。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: What did you dream about last night?
sentences.zh: 你昨晚梦见了什么？

sentences.en: I don't even really remember.
sentences.zh: 我其实都不太记得了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I always forget my dreams too.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我也总是忘记我的梦。

sentences.en: I try sometimes to write them down so I can remember them.
sentences.zh: 我有时会试着把它们写下来，这样我就能记住了。

sentences.en: Do you ever do that?
sentences.zh: 你试过这样做吗？

sentences.en: No, ma'am.
sentences.zh: 没有，女士。

sentences.en: I'm still working on spelling, so.
sentences.zh: 我还在练习拼写呢，所以……

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 那倒也是。

sentences.en: Okay, that would probably be really hard to say Marco Babar.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那个名字叫“马可·巴巴”可能真的很难读。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Is that his last name?
sentences.zh: 那是他的姓吗？

sentences.en: Marco Babar?
sentences.zh: 马可·巴巴？

sentences.en: Barbaro, yeah.
sentences.zh: 巴巴罗，是的。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So why don't we try it?
sentences.zh: 那我们为什么不试一下呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: For the New York Times, I'm Ella.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的埃拉。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, we are talking about fears and how to face them.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来聊聊恐惧以及如何面对恐惧。

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月14日，星期五。

sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Hi, is this Ella?
sentences.zh: 嗨，是埃拉吗？

sentences.en: Um, that was my mom talking, but now it's me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，刚才是我妈妈在说话，但现在是我了。

sentences.en: Is that Michael?
sentences.zh: 是迈克尔吗？

sentences.en: Hi, Ella.
sentences.zh: 嗨，埃拉。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Are you wearing headphones?
sentences.zh: 你戴着耳机吗？

sentences.en: How does it feel?
sentences.zh: 感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: All right, cool.
sentences.zh: 好的，酷。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: Back in 2019, my colleague Julia Longoria traveled to Nashville, Tennessee, and made one of our favorite episodes, which we're re-airing today.
sentences.zh: 早在2019年，我的同事朱莉娅·朗格利亚前往田纳西州的纳什维尔，制作了我们最喜欢的节目之一，今天我们将重播这一集。

sentences.en: A conversation with Ella Maynors and her mother, Katie Maynors.
sentences.zh: 这是一段与埃拉·梅诺斯和她母亲凯蒂·梅诺斯的对话。

sentences.en: It feels okay?
sentences.zh: 感觉还可以吗？

sentences.en: Yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 是的，先生。

sentences.en: Are you calling me sir?
sentences.zh: 你在叫我先生吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, sir.
sentences.zh: 是的，先生。

sentences.en: You don't have to do that.
sentences.zh: 你不用那样称呼我。

sentences.en: I appreciate it, but...
sentences.zh: 我很感激，但是……

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 知道了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: How are you hearing me through this microphone?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么通过这个麦克风听到我说话的？

sentences.en: I'm not actually hearing you through the microphone.
sentences.zh: 其实我不是通过麦克风听到你说话的。

sentences.en: I'm hearing you through the phone, but then eventually, a lot of people are going to hear you through the microphone.
sentences.zh: 我是通过电话听到你说话的，但最终，很多人会通过麦克风听到你的声音。

sentences.en: I don't get it.
sentences.zh: 我不明白。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't get it either.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我也不明白。

sentences.en: I thought that we might begin with just a couple of really basic questions.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以先从几个非常基本的问题开始。

sentences.en: How old are you?
sentences.zh: 你多大了？

sentences.en: I just turned nine.
sentences.zh: 我刚满九岁。

sentences.en: And since you're in, Ella, your bedroom, I wonder if you could describe a little bit of your surroundings, just a couple of things in that room that mean something to you.
sentences.zh: 既然你在你的卧室里，埃拉，我想请你描述一下周围的环境，说说房间里对你有意义的几样东西。

sentences.en: Everybody in here.
sentences.zh: 这里的所有人。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: My bunk bed and my stuffed animals.
sentences.zh: 我的双层床和我的毛绒玩具。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about those stuffed animals?
sentences.zh: 能跟我说说那些毛绒玩具吗？

sentences.en: I got a unicorn named Uni, and Bun Bun is my favorite, which is a bunny.
sentences.zh: 我有一个叫“尤尼”的独角兽，还有我最喜欢的“蹦蹦”，它是一只兔子。

sentences.en: She has OCD.
sentences.zh: 她有强迫症。

sentences.en: Bun Bun has obsessive compulsive disorder.
sentences.zh: 蹦蹦患有强迫症。

sentences.en: Yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 是的，先生。

sentences.en: I mean, yes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的。

sentences.en: So, Ella, I know that you have been through a lot this last year, so I wanted to talk about that with you and with your mom.
sentences.zh: 埃拉，我知道你去年经历了很多，所以我很想和你以及你妈妈聊聊这件事。

sentences.en: Does that sound fine?
sentences.zh: 这样可以吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Let me start by asking you about your biggest fears.
sentences.zh: 让我先问问你最大的恐惧是什么。

sentences.en: What are you most scared of?
sentences.zh: 你最害怕什么？

sentences.en: Um, throwing up, tornadoes, fires, wind decks, monsters, and going upstairs by myself or in the garage.
sentences.zh: 嗯，呕吐、龙卷风、火灾、风暴、怪物，还有独自上楼或去车库。

sentences.en: And among those, because that's a fair number of fears, what would you say are the biggest, the things that you're most afraid of?
sentences.zh: 在这些恐惧中，因为恐惧的数量不少，你会说哪一个是最大的，你最害怕的是什么？

sentences.en: Getting sick.
sentences.zh: 生病。

sentences.en: And, like, tornadoes.
sentences.zh: 还有，比如龙卷风。

sentences.en: We have, like, tornado watches here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里经常有龙卷风预警。

sentences.en: Desert tornado.
sentences.zh: 沙漠龙卷风。

sentences.en: And the worst thing is, our tornado siren is right beside our house.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的是，我们的龙卷风警报器就在我们房子旁边。

sentences.en: So you can hear it, like, really clear.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以听得非常清楚。

sentences.en: It's loud.
sentences.zh: 声音很大。

sentences.en: It's really loud.
sentences.zh: 真的很大声。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It's a twister.
sentences.zh: 是龙卷风。

sentences.en: It's a twister.
sentences.zh: 是龙卷风。

sentences.en: It's like the apocalypse is coming.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像世界末日要来了。

sentences.en: Like, that's just kind of where her mind goes.
sentences.zh: 这就是她脑子里想的事情。

sentences.en: But we have never had a tornado actually hit our house.
sentences.zh: 但我们从来没有真正遇到过龙卷风袭击我们的房子。

sentences.en: That's good.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: Yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 是的，先生。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Obsessive compulsive disorder is not what I imagined it to be.
sentences.zh: 强迫症并不是我想象中的那样。

sentences.en: I pictured mainly the compulsive side of OCD.
sentences.zh: 我主要想象的是强迫症的强迫行为那一面。

sentences.en: Hand washing over and over, checking locks, or things like that.
sentences.zh: 一遍又一遍地洗手、检查门锁之类的东西。

sentences.en: And with Ella, in particular, her OCD focuses more on the obsession, obsessive thoughts of vomiting, of tornadoes.
sentences.zh: 而对于埃拉来说，她的强迫症更多地集中在强迫观念上，比如对呕吐、龙卷风的强迫性思维。

sentences.en: Ella's compulsion is actually avoidance.
sentences.zh: 埃拉的强迫行为实际上是回避。

sentences.en: She will do anything to avoid the situations where vomit, tornado, could happen.
sentences.zh: 她会尽一切努力去避免那些可能发生呕吐或龙卷风的情况。

sentences.en: OCD is just something that telling you that scary things are going to happen to you.
sentences.zh: 强迫症只是在告诉你，可怕的事情将会发生在你身上。

sentences.en: It took what Ella had a fear of.
sentences.zh: 它抓住了埃拉恐惧的东西。

sentences.en: Vomit, tornadoes.
sentences.zh: 呕吐、龙卷风。

sentences.en: And just made that fear just enormous.
sentences.zh: 然后把这种恐惧变得无限巨大。

sentences.en: When I found out that I had OCD, I feel like it changed my life a lot.
sentences.zh: 当我发现自己患有强迫症时，我觉得它彻底改变了我的生活。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: It was harder for me to do a lot of different stuff that other people can do, and it was just harder, I feel like.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，做很多别人能做的事情变得更难了，我觉得一切都变得更困难了。

sentences.en: The first time, it was just your typical school day.
sentences.zh: 第一次，那只是一个普通的上学日。

sentences.en: And I get to the carpool line at school, and I drive up, and instead of Ella walking to her car, her teacher dies.
sentences.zh: 我开车到了学校的拼车接送区，结果埃拉没有走向她的车，她的老师却过来了。

sentences.en: And I kind of rolled down the window, a little confused, going like, okay, where's Ella?
sentences.zh: 我摇下车窗，有点困惑，心想，好吧，埃拉在哪儿？

sentences.en: Ella, and that's when she told me, Ella won't leave the classroom.
sentences.zh: 埃拉，就在那时她告诉我，埃拉不肯离开教室。

sentences.en: And of course I'm going, what do you mean she won't leave the classroom?
sentences.zh: 我当然会问，你是什么意思，她为什么不肯离开教室？

sentences.en: And when I got to her classroom, she was literally, um...
sentences.zh: 当我赶到她的教室时，她真的……

sentences.en: I just remember I was, like, screaming on the floor.
sentences.zh: 我只记得我当时在地上尖叫。

sentences.en: If I moved, I was going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 如果我动一下，我就会吐出来。

sentences.en: Knees up to her chest, arms wrapped around her.
sentences.zh: 双膝蜷缩到胸前，双臂紧紧抱着自己。

sentences.en: She was tucked into a little ball.
sentences.zh: 她缩成了一个小球。

sentences.en: And she was just laying on the floor, crying.
sentences.zh: 她就那样躺在地上哭。

sentences.en: And she was able to say, like, if I move, I think I'm going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 她当时能说出来的话是，如果我动一下，我觉得我会吐。

sentences.en: Or if I stand up, I'm going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 或者如果我站起来，我就会吐。

sentences.en: There was not one thing I could say.
sentences.zh: 我当时什么话也说不出来。

sentences.en: You're going to be okay.
sentences.zh: 你会没事的。

sentences.en: You know, you're not going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不会生病的。

sentences.en: That helped her.
sentences.zh: 那对她有帮助。

sentences.en: She was just stuck.
sentences.zh: 她只是卡住了。

sentences.en: Her brain was stuck.
sentences.zh: 她的大脑卡住了。

sentences.en: On this one thought of, I'm going to get sick, Ella was basically paralyzed with her fear.
sentences.zh: 在那一个“我会生病”的念头上，埃拉基本上被她的恐惧瘫痪了。

sentences.en: And I ended up just having to literally pull her off the floor and carry her to my car.
sentences.zh: 最后我不得不把她从地上拉起来，抱到我的车里。

sentences.en: I am going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 我要吐了。

sentences.en: We didn't know that the things we were doing, the reassuring her, you know, you're not going to get sick, those were really amplifying her OCD.
sentences.zh: 我们当时不知道我们所做的事情，比如安慰她“你不会生病的”，实际上是在加剧她的强迫症。

sentences.en: And the next thing that really pushed us was the day we got the phone call from the principal that told me there had been just a routine tornado drill at school.
sentences.zh: 接下来真正推动我们的是那天接到校长的电话，告诉我学校进行了一次例行的龙卷风演习。

sentences.en: Ella, can you tell me what happened that day?
sentences.zh: 埃拉，你能告诉我那天发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Um, well, it was cold outside, so I was wearing two jackets.
sentences.zh: 嗯，外面很冷，所以我穿了两件外套。

sentences.en: The tornado drill was at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 龙卷风演习是在放学前进行的。

sentences.en: Hearing the siren really just kind of sent Ella into that state of all-consuming fear.
sentences.zh: 听到警报声真的让埃拉陷入了那种吞噬一切的恐惧状态。

sentences.en: I was telling myself, like, no, I'm not going to get sick.
sentences.zh: 我一直在告诉自己，不，我不会吐的。

sentences.en: So you kind of tried to talk yourself out of it.
sentences.zh: 所以你试着说服自己不要那样想。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I didn't take the two coats off, and it was, like, really hot inside.
sentences.zh: 我没有脱掉那两件外套，里面真的很热。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And it was really thick coats.
sentences.zh: 而且那是很厚的外套。

sentences.en: And we had to duck our heads down, even though it was just fake.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不低下头，尽管那只是演习。

sentences.en: We were, so I just make sure we knew what to do.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在做，所以我只是确保我们知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: And what did you do?
sentences.zh: 那你做了什么？

sentences.en: Um, I went to the bathroom with everybody.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我和大家一起去了洗手间。

sentences.en: We ducked our head in, and, like, then, um, and then I threw up.
sentences.zh: 我们探头进去，然后，嗯，接着我就吐了。

sentences.en: I mean, when they told me, it was like, oh, my gosh, like, poor child.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当他们告诉我的时候，我就觉得，天哪，这孩子真可怜。

sentences.en: How much worse could it get?
sentences.zh: 还能有多糟糕呢？

sentences.en: It had to be a tornado, and it had to be vomit.
sentences.zh: 偏偏是龙卷风，偏偏又吐了。

sentences.en: It was her two worst fears in one.
sentences.zh: 这简直是她最害怕的两件事撞到了一起。

sentences.en: And what did that experience do to your fears?
sentences.zh: 那次经历对你的恐惧感有什么影响？

sentences.en: It just made them worse, really.
sentences.zh: 真的，只会让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: These fears just kind of consumed her.
sentences.zh: 这些恐惧几乎吞噬了她。

sentences.en: They kind of consumed her life.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎吞噬了她的生活。

sentences.en: There have been some boys that bullied me before.
sentences.zh: 以前有些男生欺负过我。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what kinds of things they would say?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我他们会说些什么吗？

sentences.en: Somebody has said to me, like, you're not that good as, like, other people because you have OCD.
sentences.zh: 有人对我说，因为你有强迫症，所以你不如别人好。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's horrible.
sentences.zh: 那太可怕了。

sentences.en: I started crying.
sentences.zh: 我当时就哭了。

sentences.en: When you start to see her not be able to do the things that she's been able to do, is when, as a parent, you go, okay, we've really got to get on this.
sentences.zh: 当你开始发现她无法再做以前能做的事情时，作为父母，你就会意识到，好吧，我们真的得重视起来了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I realized that we had to do it the hard way.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我们必须得走那条艰难的路。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What do you mean the hard way?
sentences.zh: 你说的“艰难的路”是指什么？

sentences.en: I don't really know.
sentences.zh: 我其实也不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: What's up?
sentences.zh: 怎么了？

sentences.en: And I second, can, do you want to talk about yourself so I can have a break?
sentences.zh: 而且，我能不能……你想聊聊你自己吗？这样我也能休息一下？

sentences.en: Do you want a break, Ella?
sentences.zh: 你想休息一下吗，艾拉？

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 拜托了。

sentences.en: Yeah, Ella, if you want a break, I would completely understand.
sentences.zh: 好的，艾拉，如果你想休息，我完全理解。

sentences.en: Take a break.
sentences.zh: 休息一下吧。

sentences.en: Right now?
sentences.zh: 现在吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, go for it.
sentences.zh: 对，去吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Don't leave.
sentences.zh: 别走开。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: So, I was kind of panicking.

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean what kind of light do they require because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 我是指他们需要什么样的光线，因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
